title: TUI is a 3,157-line monolith
description: tui.py mixes UI rendering, data loading, agent management, and server communication in one 3,157-line file. Hard to test or maintain. The _check_for_changes() method also stats every feature file on each refresh cycle, which won't scale. Should be split into separate modules for each concern.

Ideation:
The core problem is that tui.py has grown to ~4,300 lines as a monolithic PipelineApp class, making it difficult to navigate, test, and maintain. The file has natural seams that suggest a multi-tier extraction strategy: Tier 1 (zero-risk) extracts pure standalone helper functions (lines 84-481) with no PipelineApp dependencies into a tui_helpers.py module; Tier 2 (low-risk) extracts free async action functions that accept a PipelineApp instance into focused action modules (e.g., tui_item_actions.py, tui_board_actions.py); Tier 3 (higher-risk) tackles modal subclasses, which are tightly coupled to PipelineApp's reactive attributes and require careful interface design.

The primary risk is not choosing wrong module boundaries—multiple defensible decompositions exist—but rather migration safety when refactoring a file with minimal test coverage. Silently broken behavior is the real danger. Before any structural extraction, a behavioral characterization test suite should be added: snapshot tests for key screen renders, integration tests that drive the TUI through critical flows (item creation, phase transitions, modal interactions), and regression guards for the most common user paths. This test harness transforms the refactor from a risky rewrite into a verifiable series of safe moves.

Key tradeoffs to consider: the 'free async functions accepting PipelineApp' pattern for action modules is pragmatic and minimizes immediate disruption, but risks recreating a God Object anti-pattern in disguise since every extracted function retains implicit access to all 30+ reactive attributes. A cleaner long-term architecture would define explicit data transfer objects or narrow interfaces (e.g., a BoardDataStore protocol) that each action module depends on—but this level of abstraction should be deferred until after Tier 1 and Tier 2 extractions prove out the basic module boundaries. The modal subclasses (Tier 3) are genuinely the most complex because they mix UI widget construction, event handling, and business logic; these should be extracted last, only after the simpler tiers establish confidence in the refactoring approach.

The recommended sequencing is: (1) add characterization tests first, (2) extract pure helpers with no behavior changes and verify tests pass, (3) extract action free-functions one module at a time with continuous test validation, (4) revisit modal extraction only if the prior tiers demonstrate the approach is working cleanly. Each step should be committed independently so any regression is immediately attributable. The goal is a file structure where tui.py contains only the PipelineApp class wiring and Textual lifecycle methods, with domain logic distributed across purpose-specific modules.
